text:
The trade request that hung over Detroit all season ended Monday in Montreal. The Canadiens acquired Dylan Larkin from the Red Wings, and Daily Faceoff reports he makes his debut tonight against the Kings. Larkin and GM Kent Hughes spent the day presenting it as a long mutual interest, as The Athletic's Arpon Basu put it; Daily Faceoff called his change of heart "a bit too convenient." Either way, the saga is over, and the Bell Centre gets him first. Our projections were built before the deal, so nothing in tonight's numbers counts him.

He joins a team that has outrun its chances. Montreal has 32 points on 24.8 our numbers say it deserved, at 51% of the five-on-five expected goals (expected goals measure the quality of chances), mostly because Jacob Fowler has been brilliant. Fowler sits tonight. Jakub Dobes starts, at .864 and 3.6 goals below expected in nine games, a year after he finished 17.3 above. Saturday's 4-3 loss to the Flyers, decided by Noah Cates with 31 seconds left, came with Nick Suzuki sending what one headline called a blunt message about letting Fowler down. Ivan Demidov (ankle), Chris Kreider (out until about January), Mike Matheson and Josh Anderson are all out, and Juraj Slafkovský has gone 15 games without a goal on 5.0 expected.

The Kings are the opposite story: a -13 goal difference on +1.7 expected, sunk by finishing and by Darcy Kuemper (.885, 5.2 goals below expected). Our numbers give them a 28% playoff chance. Artemi Panarin is cleared from the injury report, Kevin Fiala is back nine months after his Olympic injury, and Quinton Byfield is one point from 200. Drew Doughty plays his 1,300th game, with his own contract talk running in the background. Corey Perry, on the fourth line but with the most dangerous shots of any depth forward over his last ten, is one of our Sleepers.
headline: Dylan Larkin's first night in a Canadiens sweater
